newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end easier with nervous eyes on Dow.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end easier with nervous eyes on Dow.

text.p: Italian stocks closed slightly lower on Friday as investors nervously eyed Wall Street, but the market ended at the day's highs as U.S. stocks edged head after Thursday's plunge and domestic bonds moved into a late rally.
"It has been a day of watching markets abroad as Wall Street rallied and Milan stocks managed to finish on the day's highs," said one Milan share trader.

All-share Mibtel index ended off 0.35 percent at 10,124 while the blue-chip Mib30 was down 0.22 percent down at 15,082. Traders said that international investors had their focus elsewhere and activity in Italian shares was light.
"We are very much at the mercy of the international situation, and the rally on the Dow and BTP bonds certainly helped the market to the day's best levels at the close," the trader added.

Among the blue-chips, Olivetti was off 2.26 percent at 505.5 lire on talk about restructuring concerning its major shareolder CIR, while ENI was off 1.01 percent at 7,574 lire and Pirelli was down 0.73 percent at 2,702 lire.
Banking stocks were largely mixed after three of Italy's major banks said there were to cut their own interest rates over the last 24 hours.

San Paolo which cut its rates late Thursday ended up 2.26 percent at 9,468 lire, BCI and Ambroveneto which cut their rates today, closed off 0.7 percent at 2,695 lire and up 1.37 percent at 3,702 lire respectively.

TV and advertising group Mediaset said it had signed an accord with U.S. telephone company GTE and Norway's Telenor, with a view to them being shareholders in a future consortium to bid for Italy's third mobile phone licence.
Mediaset shares ended off 0.04 percent at 6,997 lire.
